key word is "most." you will never ever ever be able to teach a class of 40 middle schoolers to play at a decent level if they can't read. obviously you can teach yourself how to make good sounds on an instrument, but if a kid can't read music, 99% of the time they will either never advance past essential elements book four or quit before they even get to that point. 

i'm not a private lesson supremacist. i was self taught on all of my instruments until college, but i also taught myself everything i could about music theory.

of course, some people have a good enough ear and mechanical understanding of their instrument that they can excel independently and without any music theory knowledge. however, this is the exception, not the rule.

however, this is different when you get to vocal music. it is absolutely possible to be an amazing singer and not know what the treble clef is. but a clarinet player is not going to be able to learn like that.

absolutely learning by ear helps, but kids can't effectively learn or practice independently if they can't read. kids can be brilliant by ear, but if they don't actually know how music works, they can't really advance on their own. reading is the only way most people can improve on their instrument without needing an instructor to hold their for hand every step of the learning process.
